## Discriminatory strategies {.smaller}

<br>

**Parity (P):** Equal division between ingroup and outgroup member

**Maximum joint profit (MJP):** Giving away as many points to the others in total


::: {.fragment}
<br>
**Maximum ingroup profit (MIP):** Giving as many points as possible to ingroup members in absolute terms

**Maximum differentiation (MD) or “winning”:** Difference between ingroup and outgroup members as large as possible
:::

::: {.fragment}
<br>
**Favouritism (FAV):** Combination of MD and MIP
:::

```{r}
#| label: pull-score-examples
#| include: false

pull_examples <- tribble(
  ~Discrimination, ~Pull, ~Intensity,
  "Outgroup", 4, "Low",
  "Outgroup", 8, "Medium", 
  "Outgroup", 12, "High",
  "None", 0, "None",
  "Ingroup", -4, "Low",
  "Ingroup", -8, "Medium",
  "Ingroup", -12, "High"
) |>
  mutate(
    Discrimination = factor(Discrimination,
                           levels = c("Outgroup", "None", "Ingroup")),
    Intensity = factor(Intensity,
                      levels = c("High", "Medium", "Low", "None"))
  )
pull_examples
```

```{r}
pull_examples |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Discrimination, y = Pull, 
             color = Discrimination, alpha = Intensity)) +
  geom_point(size = 5) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("High" = 1.0, "Medium" = 0.7, "Low" = 0.4, 
                                "None" = 1.0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-12, 12), breaks = seq(-12, 12, 4))
```
